title: Derived pullback commutes with closed pushforward in a Tor-independent square
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes and let $f:X'\to X$ be any scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Form $Z'=Z\times_X X'$ with projections $g:Z'\to Z$ and $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume $i$ and $f$ are stalkwise Tor independent: for every $z\in Z$ and $x'\in X'$ with $i(z)=f(x')=x$, one has $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{X,x}}_n(\mathcal O_{Z,z},\mathcal O_{X',x'})=0$ for every $n>0$ [def-pc-pullback-stalk-tensor-comparison, def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Then for every $K\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ the canonical derived base-change map is an isomorphism, naturally in $K$:
$$Lf^*Ri_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri'_*Lg^*K\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_{X'})$$
[def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Here the comparison is the adjoint of $Lg^*Li^*Ri_*K\to Lg^*K$, obtained from the pullback composition identification and the counit $Li^*Ri_*K\to K$. No boundedness, quasi-coherence, Noetherianity or finiteness assumption is imposed. Use the composition identification of [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] and the derived adjunction of [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint-general].

source.place: Tag 0E23, lemma-compare-base-change-closed-immersion; canonical comparison and all unbounded K explicitly in its proof

proof.text: Let $\beta_K$ be the canonical mate specified in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-closed-immersion-derived-exchange-stalk-formula]. At $x'=i'(z')$, write $z=g(z')$, $x=i(z)$ and $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $A=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X',x'}$, $C=\mathcal O_{Z',z'}$. It identifies $C$ with $A\otimes_R B$ and identifies the stalk of this very mate with the canonical ring comparison for $M=K_z$. Outside $i'(Z')$ both stalk objects vanish.

Choose an $A$-K-flat complex $Q$ representing $M$, and an $R$-K-flat complex $P$ with a quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to Q|_R$, using [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution] twice. By [lem-pc-affine-derived-base-change-comparison-map], the stalk comparison is represented in $D(B)$ by
$$P\otimes_R B\xrightarrow{s\otimes1}Q\otimes_R B\cong Q\otimes_A(A\otimes_R B).$$
The last isomorphism sends $q\otimes b$ to $q\otimes(1\otimes b)$, with inverse $q\otimes(a\otimes b)\mapsto aq\otimes b$; these commute with the differentials since the rings are in degree zero.

The assumed stalkwise Tor independence gives $\operatorname{Tor}_n^R(A,B)=0$ for every $n>0$ for this pair $(z,x')$. All the hypotheses of [lem-pc-tor-independent-kflat-resolution-tensor] now hold for $Q,P,s$: it makes $s\otimes_R B$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the ring comparison, and hence $(\beta_K)_{x'}$, is invertible in $D(B)$, since quasi-isomorphisms are inverted in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Neither complex was truncated.

source.place: Tag 0661, lemma-base-change-comparison, applied as in Tag 0E23

proof.text: Every stalk comparison is invertible: Step 3 handles the closed image, and Step 1 gives $0\to0$ elsewhere. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], stalks commute with kernels and images and therefore with each cohomology sheaf. Thus every $H^n(\beta_K)$ is an isomorphism on all stalks; [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] makes it an isomorphism of module sheaves. The unbounded criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] makes $\beta_K$ invertible. The mate construction is natural in $K$; inverses are natural by multiplying its naturality equation by the two component inverses.
